summary:
The owner's "Adobe suite clone" is almost certainly ArtCraft. It is a set of seven open-source rebuilds of Adobe apps (PhotoCraft, VectorCraft, FilmCraft, EffectCraft, DesignCraft and others), written in Rust under MIT/Apache-2.0, for macOS, Windows and Linux, with some apps in the browser. It was released around early October 2026 (itproexpert.com, 8 Oct 2026; getartcraft.com; github.com/storytold). Only one source confirms it, and all seven apps are early alpha. None of them builds websites, so it is useful only as the idea: a simple Photoshop/After-Effects-style tool for marketing people, with layers, a canvas, guides and a timeline. It is not something to embed.

servd already has the storefront module, so there is nothing new to build alongside it (standing rule: flag duplicates). Admin → Storefront (/storefront) is the only content editor. It has a 3-pane builder (palette, canvas, inspector), pop-up rules, a Library, CEO approval, versions/rollback and A/B, all over one Block[] JSON. Three renderers read that JSON: the storefront PageRenderer, the mobile BlockRenderer and backend zod. But the "canvas" is a list of rows with drag-to-reorder, not a picture of the page. You only see the real page in a separate Preview tab (30-min token). There is no free placement, no resize handles, no alignment guides, and the only scroll animation is a one-shot entrance effect (fade-up and so on). That explains why the owner experiences it as "doesn't work" or not for dummies.

A likely hard failure too: the builder will not open a page until it has fetched the section catalogue cross-origin from NEXT_PUBLIC_STOREFRONT_URL (default https://servd.pk)/api/storefront-sections. So when servd.pk is down (it is now) or ADMIN_ORIGINS doesn't match, every page shows only an error. The screenshot was not available, so this is unconfirmed.

Recommendation: Option A plus a small piece of C. Turn the existing builder into a visual editor that shows the real storefront page in an iframe, over the SAME block JSON. Add a freeform "Design canvas" block for Canva-style drag, resize and snap inside a band. Add scroll animations as a typed `motion` property on every block, picked from presets with an optional keyframe timeline. The web renders it with CSS scroll-driven animations plus a small JS fallback; mobile renders it with RN Animated driven by scroll, and falls back to the entrance animation where it can't. GrapesJS, Puck and Craft.js should not be adopted as the editor. They bring their own document model, which would break mobile native rendering, the sections contract, the brand rules and the approvals pipeline. At most, borrow ideas from them, or use Puck's UI patterns.

existing.what: The storefront content module: the only content editor (owner decision 41). Hub tabs are Pages / Pop-ups / Library / Approvals
existing.notes: Anything new must UPGRADE this, never sit beside it. The old Visual Layout, /content, /storefront-hero, /storefront-footer and /media were already folded into it (/media is now a redirect).

existing.what: Builder UI: palette + canvas + inspector, versions drawer, approvals, library
existing.where: frontend/admin/src/components/storefront/{Builder.tsx 423, Canvas.tsx 213, BlockInspector.tsx 450, SectionFields.tsx, fields.tsx, panels.tsx, tree.ts, LibraryPanel.tsx 578, ApprovalsPanel.tsx, VersionsDrawer.tsx}
existing.notes: Canvas.tsx is an ordered list of rows with native HTML5 drag-and-drop (reorder, drag from the palette, into/out of columns), not a picture of the page. Preview opens a new tab. Builder waits for BOTH edit.data AND catalog.data before showing anything (Builder.tsx ~line 92), so if the storefront is unreachable the editor never opens. Selection, undo and drag logic live in tree.ts and could be reused.

existing.what: Admin block types/palette (mirror of the storefront's)
existing.notes: Lists 19 block types (hero, text, cta_button, banner, quote, stat_strip, voices, image, gallery, video, columns, spacer, divider, kitchens, featured_menu, reviews, signup_form, waitlist_form, section). BaseBlock has background/textColor/paddingY/fullBleed/hidden/animation/animationDelayMs/animationDurationMs/fontFamily. Animation is one of 'none'|'fade-up'|'fade-in'|'slide-left'|'slide-right'|'zoom-in' and plays once on entry. No width/size/position/motion-on-scroll props.

Fetches `${STOREFRONT_URL}/api/storefront-sections` cross-origin (STOREFRONT_URL from lib/content.ts defaults to https://servd.pk). This is a single point of failure for the whole editor: prod is down, and the default URL is prod even in dev.

CORS allow-list comes from ADMIN_ORIGINS. The section contract: variant+fields, pixel-faithful defaults, everything visible is a field, safeHref/safeSrc/color, brand rules, catalogue is data only. Groups: servd, brand, stackd, simmer, flipd.

existing.what: Storefront block schema + renderer + entrance animation
existing.notes: Animate.tsx is an IntersectionObserver that plays once, honours prefers-reduced-motion, and wraps sections too. No scroll-linked (scrubbed) animation exists in the block system.

existing.what: Bespoke scroll motion inside sections (code, not editable)
existing.where: frontend/storefront/src/components/kinetic/motionHooks.ts (useScrollReveal), sections/servd/ScrollHero.tsx + ui/scroll-expansion-hero.tsx, sections/simmer/FridgeHero.tsx, sections/stackd/StackdStickers.tsx, StackdSlip.tsx, flipd/SpecHero.tsx, etc.
existing.notes: A second and third home for scroll animation, separate from block.animation. Any new motion system should absorb these as presets, or at least not add a fourth. The storefront has NO animation library dependency (no framer-motion/gsap/lenis in package.json, though CLAUDE.md mentions framer-motion).

Renders the DRAFT through the same ManagedPage/PopupPreview as live, so it is the natural basis for an in-editor live canvas. Blocker: storefront next.config.js:103 sends X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN on every route, so admin.servd.pk cannot iframe it until /preview (or a new /editor-frame) gets `frame-ancestors https://admin.servd.pk` instead.

existing.what: Backend content API: drafts, submit, CEO approve/schedule/reject, versions, rollback, A/B stats, public live/popups
existing.where: backend/src/modules/siteLayouts/{routes.ts 587, service.ts, schemas.ts}; Prisma SiteLayout / SiteLayoutVersion / SiteLayoutStat (schema.prisma ~2777)
existing.notes: Block validation is loose (passthrough), so new props like `motion`/`frame` survive saving but are not validated. The animation fields are range-checked. Limits: MAX_TOP_LEVEL_BLOCKS 80, MAX_CONTENT_BYTES 200 KB (a freeform canvas with many layers will push this). Popup rules are strict zod (kinds signup/login/offer/announcement; display modal/bar/corner; triggers before_page/after_seconds/exit_intent/scroll; audience; frequency; window).

existing.where: admin popups/[key] (Builder with PopupRulesPanel); storefront components/popups/{PopupHost.tsx,PopupBlocks.tsx} mounted in app/layout.tsx; GET /site-layouts/popups/live; mobile/src/content/PopupHost.tsx
existing.notes: Already built. 'Make sure pop-ups work' is a verification task (needs a running stack), not a rebuild. PopupHost fetches live popups client-side and filters by page patterns, brand and audience.

existing.where: frontend/admin/src/components/storefront/LibraryPanel.tsx; Prisma MediaAsset (tenantId, kind, conceptId, fontFamily); uploads via S3 presigner
existing.notes: 'Add file to element' already exists as form fields of kind image/video. What is missing is drag-a-file-onto-the-canvas and a picker opened from the canvas.

existing.what: Mobile native renderer of the same JSON
existing.notes: Renders the general block types and the entrance Animation (RN Animated, plays on mount, not on scroll-into-view). It does NOT render `section` blocks (falls through to null), so mobile already shows nothing for most designed pages. scroll.ts has a scroll-progress bus usable for scroll-linked motion. No reanimated or lottie dependency.

existing.what: Approval badge / pending queue in the shell
existing.notes: Relates to the owner's 'where is my CEO approval thing'. Storefront approvals live at /storefront?tab=approvals and are CEO-only (role admin). Making approvals reassignable to head-office HODs belongs to the separate head-office workstream, but it would change this module's CEO-only approve rule.

Storefront sits in a workspace section. Giving it to the marketing team means the Marketing workspace/module grants. No new module id is needed unless a separate 'storefront_publish' right is introduced.

gaps:
1. Probable hard failure: the editor depends on a cross-origin fetch of the section catalogue from the live storefront (default https://servd.pk). With prod down or ADMIN_ORIGINS wrong, every page editor shows only an error. Fix by serving the catalogue same-origin (a small admin Next route that proxies the storefront's internal URL, or the API caching the last good catalogue) and by letting the editor open with general elements when the catalogue is missing. This is the first thing to fix whatever is chosen.
2. No WYSIWYG: the canvas is a row list, and the real look is only in a separate Preview tab whose token expires in 30 min. Iframing the real page is blocked by X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN.
3. No direct manipulation: no select-on-page, no resize handles, no alignment guides/snapping, no free placement, no drag-a-file-onto-element, no undo/redo history visible to users (check tree.ts), and no desktop/mobile breakpoint toggle.
4. Scroll animation is entrance-only (6 presets, one shot). There is no scroll-linked/scrubbed motion (parallax, pin and reveal, scale-through, sticky stacking, horizontal scroll, text reveal, progress), no timeline, and no per-device on/off. The bespoke scroll heroes are hard-coded in section components and not editable.
5. Mobile app renders no `section` blocks at all, and its entrance animation runs on mount rather than on scroll-into-view, so mobile parity is already broken for designed pages.
6. Backend validation passes unknown props through unvalidated. A new `motion`/`frame` model needs zod bounds, or one bad value can break rendering. The 200 KB content cap may be tight for layered freeform designs.
7. Brand-rule guard rails aren't enforced in the editor (e.g. colour pickers accept any hex; nothing prevents a second orange on Simmer, white on Simmer, rectangular cards on Stackd, or a gradient). For a marketing team this needs token-only colour swatches per brand, plus a lint before submit.
8. Approvals: approval is hard-wired to role `admin` (CEO). The owner wants reassignable approvers (head-office HODs), which is a cross-cutting decision shared with the head-office work.
9. Pop-ups: built on web and mobile but unverified end to end against a running stack. There is no visual pop-up designer beyond the same row builder, and no 'test as visitor' preview of triggers.
10. Docs drift: CLAUDE.md says framer-motion/three are in the storefront lockfile, but storefront package.json has no animation libs, and storefront lib/blocks.ts header comments still point to the retired apps/web content editor.

options.option: A. Upgrade the existing builder into a visual editor over the SAME block JSON. The centre pane becomes an iframe of the real storefront renderer (/preview or a new noindex /editor-frame route allowing frame-ancestors admin.servd.pk). Blocks get data-block-id, and an overlay talks to the frame by postMessage: hover/selection boxes, drag to reorder on the page, padding/width/height handles that snap to the existing tokens (paddingY sm..xl, maxWidth narrow/wide/full, aspect), alignment guides, and drop a Library file onto an image/video slot. Keep the row list as a 'Layers' panel. Add a desktop/tablet/phone width toggle. Scroll animations become a `motion` prop on BaseBlock edited from a preset gallery with live scrub preview. Pop-ups are edited the same way in the frame's PopupPreview.
options.pros: Keeps everything that already works: approvals, scheduled publish, versions/rollback, A/B, company scoping of slugs, Library, sections contract, brand renderers, mobile JSON. No second editor and no second source of truth. What marketing sees is exactly the real storefront, with real brand CSS and live data. Can ship in slices: the fetch fix and iframe canvas first, then handles, then motion.
options.cons: Flow layout only, so no truly free 'put this anywhere' placement. Resizing means changing token sizes, not pixels. The iframe/postMessage overlay is real engineering: measuring rects across scroll, re-rendering on each edit (debounced draft render), and preview-token refresh. Server-component sections mean the first version re-renders through the server (~0.5-1.5 s per change) unless a client-render path is added.

options.option: B. Embed an off-the-shelf builder. GrapesJS (BSD-3, HTML/CSS output) or Puck (MIT, React, JSON of {type, props, zones}) or Craft.js (MIT, React node tree); register the storefront's blocks and sections as its components.
options.pros: Gets a polished drag/drop/resize/undo UI quickly (Puck especially fits React/Next and stores plain JSON). GrapesJS has the most 'Webflow-like' freeform styling, asset manager and layer manager out of the box.
options.cons: GrapesJS emits HTML/CSS: the mobile app cannot render it natively, the sections contract and brand rules (tokens, safeHref, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML) are bypassed, and user-written CSS defeats brand guard rails. Puck/Craft.js bring their own document shape, so either we convert on save (two schemas to keep in step, plus the mobile and zod copies make four) or migrate every SiteLayout row. Their in-editor rendering is not our real storefront page (brand CSS, live data, server sections) unless we wire it to our renderers anyway, which is most of option A's work. Approvals/versions/A-B must be re-plumbed. None solves scroll animation. Hosted ones (Builder.io, Plasmic) put content and approval on a third party, which doesn't fit. Webstudio (AGPL, a full Webflow alternative with its own hosting model) and Onlook (edits React source code, aimed at devs) don't fit a content-JSON + CEO-approval model. Penpot is a design tool and produces no live site.

options.option: C. Hybrid. Option A for all pages, plus one new block type, 'Design canvas' (freeform), for the Canva/Photoshop-like part. It is a band with a fixed aspect ratio per breakpoint (desktop, and a separate phone layout or auto-stack) holding layers (text, image, video, shape, button, sticker). Each layer has x/y/w/h in % of the band, rotation, z-order and opacity, plus its own `motion`. Editing happens in an admin-side canvas with snapping/alignment guides, smart distance hints, multi-select, align/distribute buttons, drag files in from the Library, lock/hide, and undo. The same block type powers pop-up layouts. Optionally borrow Puck/react-moveable-style libraries for handles only (not as the document model).
options.pros: Delivers the 'for dummies graphic design' feel the owner literally asked for (drag anywhere, resize, align, add a file) without giving up the flow-layout pages that keep SEO, accessibility and responsiveness. Percent-based layers render identically on web (absolutely positioned in an aspect-ratio box) and natively on mobile (same math in an RN View). Stays inside one schema, one approval path and one Library. Brand guard rails are easy because layers only take token colours and Library fonts.
options.cons: Freeform bands need a phone layout, or an auto-stack fallback, or they shrink unreadably. Absolutely positioned text is worse for SEO/a11y than flow content, so it should be limited to visual bands and pop-ups, not body copy. More schema, zod and mobile renderer work. Watch the 200 KB content cap. Two editing modes (flow page + freeform band) need clear UI.

recommendation:
Choose C, built on A, in phases, and do not adopt GrapesJS/Puck/Craft.js as the document model. The standing rule (one source of truth) and the mobile + approvals constraints decide it. ArtCraft (the 'Adobe clone') is the inspiration for the UX only: layers, guides, a timeline. It is not a dependency.

PHASED PLAN
This week (S-M, mostly admin + storefront, no schema migration):
(1) Make the editor open reliably. Serve the section catalogue same-origin (admin route proxying the storefront's internal URL, or the API caching the last good copy). Show general elements and a clear banner instead of a dead page when the catalogue is missing. Fix the dev default of STOREFRONT_URL.
(2) Live canvas v1. Allow `frame-ancestors https://admin.servd.pk` on /preview only (keep SAMEORIGIN elsewhere). Embed the preview in the centre pane with debounced autosave-to-draft + reload (keeping scroll position), a desktop/phone width toggle, and click-on-page-to-select via data-block-id + postMessage. Keep the row list as the Layers panel.
(3) Verify pop-ups end to end on a local stack: create, approve, then show on web with each trigger (before_page, after_seconds, exit_intent, scroll) and on mobile. Add a 'test this pop-up now' button that ignores frequency.
(4) Motion v1 = 'scroll presets' on every block (schema below) with CSS scroll-driven rendering + JS fallback, and a scrub slider in the inspector to preview it.

Next 2-3 weeks (L):
(5) Direct manipulation on the page: drag to reorder in the frame, padding/width handles that snap to tokens, alignment/centre guides, drop-a-file-from-Library onto an image/video slot, undo/redo.
(6) Brand guard rails. Colour pickers become token swatches per brand. Add a pre-submit lint (Simmer: no white/gradient/second orange/exclamation; Stackd: sticker shapes; no emoji), shown to the approver.
(7) Approvals: route to an assignable approver once the head-office/HOD decision lands. Keep 'nothing publishes without approval'.

Later (XL):
(8) 'Design canvas' freeform block (layers in %, per-breakpoint frames, snapping, align/distribute, multi-select), also used as the pop-up designer.
(9) Motion v2: a keyframe timeline per layer (opacity/x/y/scale/rotate/blur at scroll % points), pin-and-scrub scenes, and text reveal. Fold the hard-coded scroll heroes into presets where feasible.
(10) Mobile: render `section` blocks (at least generic fallbacks) and the Design canvas, so the app stops showing blank designed pages.

HOW SCROLL ANIMATION IS MODELLED (one JSON, many renderers)
Add an optional, zod-validated field to BaseBlock (and to canvas layers):
motion?: {
  enter?: 'none'|'fade-up'|'fade-in'|'slide-left'|'slide-right'|'zoom-in'|'blur-in'|'stagger-children', enterDelayMs?, enterDurationMs?,
  scroll?: { preset: 'parallax'|'fade-through'|'scale-through'|'rise'|'pin-reveal'|'sticky-stack'|'horizontal-pan'|'text-reveal'|'progress-fill', strength: 'subtle'|'medium'|'strong', range: 'entering'|'crossing'|'leaving' },
  keyframes?: Array<{ at: 0..100, opacity?, x?, y?, scale?, rotate?, blur? }>  (v2, max ~6),
  devices?: 'all'|'desktop'|'none-on-phone'
}
The existing animation* fields map to motion.enter, so old JSON keeps working, and the three type copies (storefront lib/blocks.ts, admin lib/blocks.ts, mobile types.ts) plus backend schemas.ts change together.
Web: compile presets/keyframes to CSS keyframes + `animation-timeline: view()` + `animation-range` (Chrome/Edge 115+, Safari 26+, Firefox reportedly 133+, so verify), guarded by `@supports`. A ~2 KB rAF/IntersectionObserver fallback sets a --p progress variable where it isn't supported. Pinning uses position: sticky inside a tall wrapper. GSAP ScrollTrigger is now fully free for commercial use (Webflow) and is an acceptable fallback engine for pin/stack scenes if CSS proves flaky, at about 25-45 KB, loaded only on pages that use those presets. Always honour prefers-reduced-motion (show the end state).
Mobile: interpolate RN Animated from the ScrollView offset (scroll.ts bus / Animated.event with native driver) for fade/rise/scale/parallax/keyframes. Pin, stack and horizontal-pan degrade to the enter animation, or to static, by design. Unknown presets fall back to no motion, never to hidden content.
Editor UX for non-designers: a gallery of preset tiles with looping thumbnails, three strength steps, a 'scrub' slider and 'play as you scroll' in the canvas. The keyframe timeline (v2) sits behind 'Advanced'.
questionsForOwner: Should the marketing team be able to place things anywhere on a free canvas (Canva-style), or is it enough to rearrange, resize and style page sections that always stay neatly stacked? Free placement takes weeks more and needs a separate phone layout.
Who approves website changes once head office exists: still only you, or any head-office HOD you assign (for example the marketing HOD)? Should some changes (like fixing a typo) skip approval?
On phones in the servd app, is it OK if the fancier scroll effects (pinning, sticky stacking, sideways scroll) play as a simple fade instead?
Should marketing be able to pick any colour and font, or only each brand's own colours and fonts? A locked palette stops brand-rule breaks such as white or a second orange on Simmer.
Is it OK to add one small animation library (GSAP, free for commercial use) for the most advanced scroll effects, or should we stick to built-in browser features only?
Can you resend the screenshot of the storefront module not working, or say what you saw? It may be an error loading sections because servd.pk is down, a blank page, or something else.
